ἐπὶ χειρῶν, Arab. مع. After a verb of
joining together, Dan. 11, 23.—But the
prep. עַל is more frequent in this sense.
7. Metaph. of regarding, having re-
spect to any thing; hence a) in respect
to, as to, Ex. 14, 5; comp. Gr. εἰς μὲν
ταῦτα. b) on account of, because of,
propter. Ez. 44, 7 אֶל־כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתֵיכֶם be-
cause of all your abominations; comp.
v. 6 where in the same connection is
read מִן, and v. 11 where it is בְּ. 2 Sam.
weep on account of, for any one, 2 Sam.
1, 24; שָׂחַק אֶל, הִנָּחֵם אֶל Judg. 21, 6.
c) about, concerning, of, after verbs of
speaking, narrating, as אָמַר Gen. 20, 2,
דִּבֶּר Jer. 40, 16, סִפֵּר Ps. 69, 27; also of
hearing Ez. 19, 4, שְׁמוּעָה אֶל tidings
about any thing 1 Sam. 4, 19. (Comp. in
N. T. εἰς Acts 2, 25. Eph. 5, 32.) See
also 1 Sam. 1, 27 אֶל־הַנַּעַר הַזֶּה הִתְפַּלָּלְתִּי
for (concerning) this child I prayed;
where אֶל marks also the end or object
of the prayer.
8. Metaph. also of a rule or norm, ac-
cording to, secundum; as אֶל־פִּי accord-
ing to the commandment Josh. 15, 13.
17, 4; אֶל־נָכוֹן according to the certainty,
for certain, 1 Sam. 26, 4; אֶל־הַנְּחִילוֹת ad
tibias Ps. 5, 1. 80, 1. So too after verbs
of likeness, as דָּמָה, נִמְשַׁל, q. v.
9. When put before prepositions de-
noting rest in a place, אֶל gives to them
the signif. of motion or direction to, to-
wards that place; מִחוּץ לְ without, out
of doors, but אֶל־מִחוּץ לְ to without, forth
without Lev. 4, 12, comp. foris and fo-
ras; בֵּין between, אֶל־בֵּין in between Ez.
10, 2. 31, 10. Comp. אֶל־אַחֲרֵי, אֶל־מִבֵּית,

lines.text: B) Less frequently and in a less accu-
rate use of language, but yet in many
certain and definite examples, אֶל as
Prep. is used also of rest or delay at, on,
in a place to which one has come; comp.
לְ lett. B, and also Gr. εἰς, ἐς, for ἐν, as ἐς
δόμους μένειν Soph. Aj. 80, οἴκαδε μένειν,
see Passow Gr. Lex. ἐν no. 6. Bernhardy
Gr. Synt. p. 215, 216. So in common
Engl. to home, to bed; Germ. zu Hause,
zu Leipzig; comp. vice versa also מִן at
a place, no. 3. h. In all this, however,
the idea of motion is not wholly lost,
viz. a motion which preceded.—Hence
spec.
1. at, by, near. יָשַׁב אֶל־הַשֻּׁלְחָן to sit
at table, Germ. zu Tische sitzen, 1 K.
13, 20; comp. ἐς θρόνους ἕζοντο Od. 4. 51.
Jer. 41, 12 וַיִּמְצְאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־מַיִם רַבִּים they
found him by the great waters near Gi-
beon, comp. 2 Sam. 2, 13. Bibl. Res. in
Palest. II. p. 136, 138.—1 Sam. 17, 3 the
Philistines stood by a mountain on this
side; where the same sense would be
given by מִן־הָהָר, see מִן no. 3. h. אֶל־
גִּבְעַת at the hill Josh. 5, 3. Ez. 7, 18
lines.draft: גִּבְעַת at the hill Josh. 5, 3. Ez. 7, 18
lines.reread: גִּבְעָה at the hill Josh. 5, 3. Ez. 7, 18
lines.note: The final Hebrew letter is tav (ת, with its distinctive left foot), not he, and the vowel under ayin is patach — construct form גִּבְעַת, continuing אֶל־ from the previous line (cf. Josh. 5:3 אֶל־גִּבְעַת הָעֲרָלוֹת). Reading B's absolute גִּבְעָה is wrong.

lines.reread: אֶל־כָּל־פָּנִים בּוֹשָׁה shame shall be on all
lines.note: The dot on the vav of בּוֹשָׁה sits above the letter (holem), not inside it (shureq); the printed form is בּוֹשָׁה, so Reading B is correct. Everything else (אֶל־כָּל־פָּנִים with dagesh in kaf and pe, shin dot) is identical in both readings and matches the print.

lines.text: ven;’ but as the words now stand, אֶל
follows a verb of rest. Gen. 6, 6 וַיִּתְעַצֵּב
אֶל־לִבּוֹ it grieved him AT his heart, he
felt grief in his heart; not, as Winer
renders, ‘it grieved him to his heart;’
since הִתְיַצֵּב as being intrans. does not
express the idea of penetrating into the
mind.—Hence also
3. אֶל as sometimes put before parti-
cles denoting rest in a place, does not
always change the sense; comp. above
in A. 9. 1 Sam. 21, 5 אֵין לֶחֶם חֹל אֶל־תַּחַת
יָדִי there is no common bread under my
hand. אֶל־מוּל for מוּל q. v.
Note. Other significations have been
ascribed to אֶל, which are foreign to its
true power; e. g. with, appealing to
Num. 25, 1. Josh. 11, 18, see in A. 1, 3,
but comp. in no. 6; also by, with, Jer.
